title: 13 Best Herbal Essential Oils For Bad Breath
intro: Herbal essential oils for bad breath are a type of natural remedy that involves the use of concentrated plant extracts to eliminate unpleasant mouth odors. These oils offer several benefits, including their antimicrobial properties, which help to kill bacteria that cause bad breath, as well as their ability to reduce inflammation and freshen breath. Examples of herbal essential oils that can be used to treat bad breath include peppermint oil, which has a refreshing and cooling effect, eucalyptus oil, which helps to reduce inflammation and fight bacteria, and tea tree oil, which has antiseptic properties that help to combat oral infections. Additionally, other oils such as ginger, lemon, and lavender can also be used to treat bad breath, as they have antibacterial and anti-inflammatory properties that help to freshen and soothe the mouth.

preparations.preparation_desc: Mentha x piperita essential oils have been traditionally used to treat bad breath, also known as halitosis, due to their antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory properties. The herbal preparation contains bioactive constituents such as menthone, menthol, and limonene, which help to kill bacteria in the mouth and reduce inflammation in the gums, thereby addressing the root cause of bad breath. By inhibiting the growth of Streptococcus mutans and other oral pathogens, Mentha x piperita essential oils help to maintain a healthy oral microbiome and prevent the formation of volatile sulfur compounds that cause bad breath. The benefits of using Mentha x piperita essential oils to treat bad breath include fresh breath, reduced gum inflammation, and a lower risk of oral infections.
preparations.preparation_study: According to "Phytotherapy research : PTR", Mentha x piperita essential oils may be beneficial for bad breath due to their antibacterial properties which are attributed to the presence of bioactive phytochemicals such as flavonoids, phenolics, lignans, stilbenes and essential oils.

preparations.preparation_desc: Eucalyptus globulus essential oils have been traditionally used to treat bad breath due to their antibacterial, anti-inflammatory, and decongestant properties. The antiseptic properties of eucalyptol, a bioactive constituent of this essential oil, help to reduce the growth of bacteria in the mouth, thus alleviating bad breath. By reducing inflammation in the gums and mouth, eucalyptus globulus essential oils also help to prevent bad breath caused by gum disease and other oral infections. The benefits of using eucalyptus globulus essential oils to treat bad breath include a reduction in bacteria, inflammation, and odor, resulting in fresher breath and improved oral health.

Zingiber officinale essential oils, extracted from the rhizomes of the ginger plant, possess potent antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory properties that help to treat bad breath or halitosis. The bioactive constituents, including gingerols and shogaols, exhibit strong antibacterial and antifungal activities, inhibiting the growth of odor-causing microorganisms in the mouth. By reducing inflammation and suppressing the growth of these microorganisms, Zingiber officinale essential oils help to alleviate bad breath, promoting a healthy oral environment. The benefits of using Zingiber officinale essential oils to treat bad breath include improved oral hygiene, reduced plaque formation, and a fresher, more confident smile.
preparations.preparation_study: According to "Pakistan journal of pharmaceutical sciences", Zingiber officinale essential oils may help combat bad breath due to the presence of significant antioxidant activity and phytochemicals, particularly total flavonoid and polyphenol contents, which were found to be highest in Zingiber officinale.

preparations.preparation_desc: Cymbopogon citratus essential oils, also known as lemon grass oil, have been traditionally used to treat bad breath due to its antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory properties. These properties help to reduce the growth of bacteria in the mouth, thereby eliminating the underlying cause of bad breath. The bioactive constituents of lemon grass oil, including citral and limonene, have been shown to exhibit antibacterial and antifungal activities, making it an effective treatment for this ailment. The use of Cymbopogon citratus essential oils as a mouthwash or in combination with other herbal preparations has been found to provide relief from bad breath and promote overall oral health.
preparations.preparation_study: According to "Antibiotics (Basel, Switzerland)", Cymbopogon citratus essential oils have been found to have in vitro antimicrobial and antibiofilm activity, specifically against Candida spp. in the oral cavity, making it a potential agent in preventing and treating oral infections, including those causing bad breath.

preparations.preparation_desc: Rosmarinus officinalis essential oils, derived from the leaves of the rosemary plant, have been traditionally used to treat bad breath due to their antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory properties. The bioactive constituents present in this herbal preparation, including camphor, bornyl acetate, and alpha-pinene, help to inhibit the growth of bacteria responsible for causing bad breath. By reducing the microbial load in the oral cavity, Rosmarinus officinalis essential oils help to alleviate bad breath and promote a healthy oral environment. The benefits of using this herbal preparation to treat bad breath include its natural and non-invasive approach, which can be used in conjunction with other oral hygiene practices to maintain fresh breath and overall oral health.
preparations.preparation_study: According to "PloS one", Rosmarinus officinalis essential oils exhibited moderate to high antibiofilm activity against Streptococcus mutans, a microorganism commonly associated with bad breath, and were shown to inhibit biofilm formation at a concentration of 1.25 mg ml-1.

preparations.preparation_desc: Thymus vulgaris essential oils, also known as thyme oil, have been used for centuries to treat bad breath due to their antimicrobial and antioxidant properties. The bioactive constituents of thyme oil, including thymol, carvacrol, and linalool, help to combat the bacteria that cause bad breath, reducing the severity of the condition. By inhibiting the growth of oral pathogens and reducing inflammation, thyme oil helps to freshen breath and promote a healthy oral environment. The benefits of using thyme oil to treat bad breath include its natural antibacterial properties, ease of use, and lack of side effects, making it a popular alternative to conventional mouthwashes and breath fresheners.
preparations.preparation_study: According to "Journal of dentistry (Shiraz, Iran)", Thymus vulgaris essential oils may help in reducing bad breath by having favorable antimicrobial activity against C. albicans, a type of microorganism that can cause oral infections and bad breath.

preparations.preparation_study: According to "Scientific reports", Salvia officinalis essential oils for bad breath have shown significant antimicrobial effects, specifically exhibiting bactericidal activities against Proteus mirabilis and Bacillus subtilis at low concentrations, which may help alleviate bad breath.
